In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
1H MR spectroscopic imaging (MRSI) of the breast is not yet ready to be implemented as a clinical tool in routine clinical practice.
1H MR spectroscopic imaging is a useful tool for the evaluation of breast lesions before biopsy, especially when the conventional MR imaging features are equivocal or inconclusive.
1H MR spectroscopic imaging and diffusion-weighted MR imaging are not currently useful tools for characterising breast lesions before biopsy.
